name: The Ashen Bargain
intro: The Ashen Wastes remember every army that burned there. Walk with the dead long enough, and something older than the Ashwalker will notice you.

steps.label: Win 3 battles with a deck that is at least 30% undead or ashen cards
Defeat The Ashwalker (Act III — The Ashen Wastes)

name: The Refracted Codex
intro: Somewhere in the Crystal Spire's misfiled archives is the schematic for a wyrm made of pure refraction. The Archivist insists it does not exist. He is lying.

steps.label: Defeat The Archivist (Act IV — The Crystal Spire)

name: Doctrine of Iron
intro: Warlord Kragg's engineers began one final war machine before the Iron Citadel fell. The blueprints survived. The discipline to finish it is the real test.

steps.label: Defeat Warlord Kragg (Act II — The Iron Citadel)

name: The Verdant Oath
intro: The oldest tree in the Verdant Shard predates the Dominion itself. Prove the forest can trust you with an army, and it will lend you something that walks.

steps.label: Win 3 battles with a deck that is at least 30% forest or canopy cards
Defeat The Thornlord (Act I — The Verdant Shard)

name: Tides of the Deep
intro: The Sunken Reef's deep-court keeps a leviathan chained beneath the throne. The Tidal Sovereign will not free it. You can take the matter up with the Sovereign directly.

steps.label: Defeat The Tidal Sovereign (Act V — The Sunken Reef)

name: The Wyvern Accord
intro: The Sky Dominion does not welcome climbers. Prove your fleet can hold formation at altitude, and the wyvern packs that circle the Cloudmarshal's spires might let you land instead of fall.

steps.label: Win 4 battles with a deck that is at least 30% sky cards
Defeat The Cloudmarshal (Act VI — The Sky Dominion)

name: The Eternal Flame
intro: Somewhere beneath the Emberfall Peaks a forge has burned, untended, since before the Fracture. The Cinderwarlord claims it answers only to him. He has never actually tried to stop it burning for someone else.

steps.label: Defeat The Cinderwarlord (Act VII — The Emberfall Peaks)

name: The Spore Ascendant
intro: The Root Queen rules the Fungal Deep from a throne the network itself grew for her. Take her seat, and the mycelium below will remember your footsteps as clearly as it remembers hers.

steps.label: Win 4 battles with a deck that is at least 30% fungal or spore cards
Defeat The Root Queen (Act VIII — The Fungal Deep)

name: The Hollow Below
intro: The Pale Engine's cold logic has never explained the sealed gate beneath the Frozen Expanse's deepest ice shelf. That may simply mean it has never been asked by anyone it couldn't out-calculate.

steps.label: Win 5 battles with a deck that is at least 30% frost or glacier cards
Defeat The Pale Engine (Act IX — The Frozen Expanse)

name: The Long Haul
intro: Every mercenary contract in the Sand Market eventually runs through one broker. The Dune Baron calls him a rival. Everyone else calls him the only merchant in the market who has never once been undercut.

steps.label: Defeat The Dune Baron (Act X — The Sand Market)

name: The Canopy Succession
intro: The Elder Warden has held the Verdant Canopy since before anyone's grandparents could name the trees. The forest does not crown a successor lightly. It has been watching you the whole climb up.

steps.label: Win 4 battles with a deck that is at least 30% canopy or ancient cards
Defeat The Elder Warden (Act XI — The Verdant Canopy)

name: The Harbor Ledger
intro: The Harbormaster keeps a ledger of every wreck the Shattered Coast has claimed — and every ship that ever slipped past him anyway. He is reportedly furious that the second list exists at all.

steps.label: Win 5 battles with a deck that is at least 30% wreck or storm cards
Defeat The Harbormaster (Act XII — The Shattered Coast)

name: The Vault Protocol
intro: The Grand Automaton has run the Clockwork Vaults on the same protocol for three centuries: admit no one, forget nothing, escalate forever. It has never had a reason to write a protocol for losing.

steps.label: Defeat The Grand Automaton (Act XIII — The Clockwork Vaults)

name: World's End
intro: The Fracture is not a place so much as the wound where a place used to be. Everything that has ever been lost to it is still down there, waiting — including, apparently, the thing that caused it.

steps.label: Defeat The Fracture (Finale — The Fractured Core)

name: The Marches Muster
intro: The Pale Herald's vanguard crossed the mist border with a proclamation nobody signed. Whatever answers his summons out there in the Marches has been waiting far longer than three centuries.

steps.label: Win 4 battles with a deck that is at least 30% forgotten cards
Defeat The Pale Herald (Act I — The Pale Marches)

name: The Unlit Toll
intro: The Toll Warden's ledger has no entries from outside Amarath, and he means to fix that personally, one traveller at a time. His lamps have not been lit in three hundred years. They still work.

steps.label: Defeat The Toll Warden (Act II — The Grey Causeway)

name: The Fallow Chorus
intro: Memory-wheat grows wild across the Unremembered Fields — eat enough of it and a stranger's whole life surfaces behind your eyes. The Gleaner Queen has never once left a row half-gleaned.

steps.label: Win 4 battles with a deck that is at least 30% forgotten cards
Defeat The Gleaner Queen (Act III — The Unremembered Fields)

name: The Unshelved Hour
intro: Every name the Fracture erased is shelved somewhere in the Archive, catalogued and fed. The Name-Eater insists it only keeps what the Court cannot bear to lose. One hour, it seems, was never properly filed.

steps.label: Defeat The Name-Eater (Act IV — The Archive of Names)

name: The Ember Vigil
intro: Ten thousand vigil flames light the Candle City, and the Lamplighter General enforces the rite without exception: light on the hour, snuff on the hour. One flame in the deep district has never once gone out.

steps.label: Win 5 battles with a deck that is at least 30% forgotten cards
Defeat The Lamplighter General (Act V — The Candle City)

name: The Drowned Harbor
intro: The coast came back misaligned when the Fracture healed — drowned towers now stand in a tide that shouldn't reach them. The Drowned Envoy walks with the water, and the water has always followed where he walks.

steps.label: Defeat The Drowned Envoy (Act VI — The Sunken Border)

name: The Still Reflection
intro: The Mirror Marsh holds still water that shows the world as it was before the Fracture — and something that answers when the reflection is asked a question nobody else can hear.

steps.label: Win 5 battles with a deck that is at least 30% forgotten cards
Defeat The Reflection (Act VII — The Mirror Marsh)

name: The Masked Rite
intro: The Hollow Court wears silver masks because its nobles forgot their own faces in the void. The Chamberlain keeps the ceremony running regardless — he has never once needed to clarify which gesture erases a name.

steps.label: Defeat The Chamberlain (Act VIII — The Hollow Court)

name: The Waited Season
intro: Amarath catalogued an entire winter it never got to spend before the Fracture, and stored it whole. The Frost Regent has kept it colder than any noble still standing watch, and she means to spend it all at once.

steps.label: Win 5 battles with a deck that is at least 30% forgotten cards
Defeat The Frost Regent (Act IX — The Winter That Waited)

name: The Grave Orchard
intro: The Bone Orchards grow from the kingdom's own dead, tended and genuinely loved. The Orchard Keeper has never once let a grave go undefended, and she does not consider what grows there a weapon. She is wrong.

steps.label: Defeat The Orchard Keeper (Act X — The Bone Orchards)

name: The Long Procession
intro: The Vigil Roads have been walked in procession for three centuries to keep the rite alive. The Procession Master has never once let the vigil go silent — not for weather, not for war, not for a single missing marcher.

steps.label: Win 6 battles with a deck that is at least 30% forgotten cards
Defeat The Procession Master (Act XI — The Vigil Roads)

name: The Crown Spire
intro: The Crown Reaches are the Court's last field army and the fortified approach to the capital both at once. The Pale Marshal has held this reach longer than any commander still counting banners, and the line has never once broken.

steps.label: Defeat The Pale Marshal (Act XII — The Crown Reaches)

name: The Vigil Engine
intro: Every window in the City of Vigils holds a candle, and the Vigil Queen has kept every single one lit longer than any sovereign still counting them. Somewhere beneath the capital, something keeps the count for her.

steps.label: Defeat The Vigil Queen (Act XIII — The City of Vigils)

name: The Unremembered Throne
intro: The Vigil King has held the whole of Amarath together in his own mind because no one else's would hold it, for three centuries, alone. Something in the throne room has kept vigil with him the entire time — and it was never the King.

steps.label: Defeat The Vigil King (Finale — The Throne of the Unremembered)
